title: Windows GPU unit tests job fails extracting OpenVINO packages due to locked tbb12.dll
signature: windows runner extract openvino packages expand-archive remove-item access to the path denied unauthorizedaccessexception locked dll file|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: Extract OpenVINO packages step fails: Remove-Item cannot delete tbb12.dll, Access to the path is denied (UnauthorizedAccessException).

key_errors:
Remove-Item : Cannot remove item C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll:
Access to the path 'C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll' is denied.
+ CategoryInfo          : PermissionDenied: (C:\actions-runn...b\bin\tbb12.dll:FileInfo) [Remove-Item], UnauthorizedAccessException
+ FullyQualifiedErrorId : RemoveFileSystemItemUnAuthorizedAccess,Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.RemoveItemCommand
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
root_cause: During the 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step, Expand-Archive (-Force) tries to overwrite install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll from the downloaded openvino_package.zip. On this Windows self-hosted runner the existing tbb12.dll is still locked by another process (most likely a lingering process from a prior job/step on the same reused runner, or a leftover antivirus/indexing handle), so the PowerShell Archive module's internal Remove-Item call fails with UnauthorizedAccessException before the DLL can be overwritten, aborting the whole extraction step with exit code 1. This is the same recurring Windows-runner file-locking issue already tracked in the pattern database (13 prior occurrences across unrelated commits and PRs), confirming it is an environment/runner-state problem rather than a code regression introduced by this commit.
reproduction_steps: N/A - Not reproducible outside the affected Windows self-hosted runner's exact state. Locally: run `Expand-Archive <openvino_package.zip> -DestinationPath install -Force` while another process (or an AV scanner) holds an open handle on install\runtime\3rdparty\tbb\bin\tbb12.dll to simulate the lock.
recommended_actions: Ensure the workflow fully stops/cleans up any process (e.g. previous test binaries, background scanners) that could hold a handle on files under install\ before the extract step runs.

Replace the blind Expand-Archive -Force with a step that first removes the stale install directory (or uses a fresh directory per run) so Expand-Archive does not need to overwrite locked files in place.
Add a retry-with-backoff wrapper around the extraction step specifically for UnauthorizedAccessException, since this is a transient runner-state issue, not a deterministic code bug.

Investigate the Windows self-hosted runner fleet for a recurring handle leak (e.g., antivirus real-time scan, a lingering ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe, or Windows Search indexer) that locks files in the install directory between jobs.
prevention_strategies: Make the Windows job's artifact-extraction step idempotent and resilient to locked files: clean/recreate the install directory before extraction instead of relying on -Force overwrite, and add a short retry loop (with a brief delay) around Expand-Archive/Remove-Item operations on Windows runners to absorb transient AV/indexer file locks. When editing or reviewing Windows CI job YAML that extracts/overwrites previously-installed binaries (tbb12.dll, openvino.dll, etc.), always wrap Expand-Archive/Remove-Item calls in a retry loop or pre-clean the target directory, since Windows self-hosted runners intermittently lock files via AV/indexer handles, causing UnauthorizedAccessException failures unrelated to the code change under test.
historical_context: This exact signature (514ffa2ab52ad344) has now been observed 13 times since 2026-11-09, across many unrelated commits/PRs, always on the Windows GPU unit tests job's 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step with the same tbb12.dll UnauthorizedAccessException. It is a well-established recurring Infrastructure issue, not tied to any specific code change.
